A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E-BATS work, with readable main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–E. Visual inspection confirms that v2's malformed Equation (3) is a document defect, not an extraction failure.

before.justification: v2 reports original speech-recognition benchmarks, memory measurements, ablations and sensitivity analyses, plus speech-emotion-recognition results in Appendix C.8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark tables and the experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The prompt adaptation procedure, CMA-ES optimization, three-component objective and T-EMA updates are retained. Equation (3) supplies the missing specification of the existing token-level loss; it does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate noisy LibriSpeech, CHiME-3 single and mixed conditions, CommonVoice and TEDLIUM-v2 for speech recognition. Both also include IEMOCAP speech-emotion recognition in Appendix C.8.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, 6 and 7 retain the same 13 TTA comparators, including TENT, EATA, SAR, CoTTA, CEA, SGEM, AWMC, SUTA, CSUTA, DSUTA, T3A, LAME and FOA. Comparator membership in the memory comparisons also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same datasets and splits, preprocessing, batch size of one, backbone models, WER metric, hyperparameters and stopping procedure. The supplementary experimental settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The component and reset ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, domain-complexity analysis, trivial-prediction analysis and continual-adaptation studies are unchanged. The distribution-shift and memory-scaling analyses are likewise retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 and Table 8 report the same ablation means and standard deviations over three random seeds in both versions. No uncertainty-reporting or repeated-run procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The main and appendix result entries and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, E-BATS retains CHiME-3-single WERs of 24.0 and 14.0 in Tables 1 and 2, and Appendix C.8 retains emotion-recognition accuracy of 38.8% before adaptation and 43.4% afterward.

T1.justification: In Section 3.3, v2's Equation (3) consists only of 'B.'; v3 replaces it with the token-level loss definition, summing squared source–target mean and standard-deviation differences with layer/token normalization. Other mathematical assumptions, formulas and complexity analyses remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty claim, three principal contributions, and claims about adaptation accuracy and memory efficiency.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning translation of latent distributions, confidence weighting and T-EMA are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitation concerning iterative CMA-ES latency and incomplete GPU parallelization.

D1.justification: Restored Equation (3) makes the token-loss calculation explicit, including its normalization and squared-distance terms, improving reproducibility of the existing component. Hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing, code-access information and Appendix D pseudocode are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and numbered reference entries are unchanged. References shift between pages without additions or removals.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv version and date text is updated. Prose, terminology, section order and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The full Equation (3) occupies more vertical space, causing downstream text reflow and shifting Figures 4 and 5 within their pages. The final reference spills onto a separate page; figure content, table structures and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 replaces the unusable 'B.' placeholder in Equation (3) with an explicit token-level alignment loss, resolving a concrete gap in the mathematical specification and aiding reproduction. The empirical evidence and remaining content are unchanged, making this a focused quality improvement.
